caption: We're saving for the wedding and still fighting about the takeaway number. Anyone else budgeting for two things at once?

slides.title:
How we spend
our R52 000
household income
Living in Kimberley
slides.body:
Him 29, her 27
Engaged, no kids yet
Jobs: Mine surveyor & pharmacist assistant
Combined net: R52 000 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 2 bed in Monument Heights, water, refuse
slides.body: We're renting together for the first time. Neither of us wants to admit how much bigger this is than either of our old places.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: One car, one instalment. Her Uber costs are technically cheaper — technically.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Checkers big shop, Spar top-ups, his protein habit
slides.body: He eats like he's still playing club rugby. He is not.

slides.title: Wedding fund
slides.includes: Venue deposit paid off, now saving for catering and her dress
slides.body: November next year. At this rate we'll make it, provided nothing else breaks.

slides.title: Takeaways & date nights
slides.includes: Friday sushi, Sunday not-cooking, the odd delivery
slides.body: We told each other it was maybe R1 500. It's R3 200. Neither of us was surprised, both of us were annoyed.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid x2, petrol & insurance, phone & fibre, funeral policies x2, stokvel, black tax, gym
slides.body: Fifteen thousand six hundred rand of things we've never once budgeted for as a couple, only separately.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R52 000, between two salaries. On paper that sounds like a lot. After the wedding fund it's R43 a day, each.

slides.title: We stopped guessing what the wedding was costing us
slides.body:
I uploaded both our statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction into one place.

Seeing both our takeaway spending on one screen ended the argument, if not the habit.

No bank login needed.
